# ezghcloud_load_balancer_waf (Resource)

Attaches a WAF to a load balancer, where it inspects requests to the http and https listeners. A load balancer has at most one WAF; destroying this detaches it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Inspect requests to the load balancer's http and https listeners.
resource "ezghcloud_load_balancer_waf" "web" {
  project_id       = var.project_id
  load_balancer_id = var.load_balancer_id
  waf_id           = ezghcloud_waf.web.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `load_balancer_id` (String) Load balancer (lbr_). Changing it replaces the attachment.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the load balancer and the WAF. Changing it replaces the attachment.
- `waf_id` (String) WAF (waf_) in the same project. Changing it switches the load balancer to the other WAF in place.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The load balancer's ID (lbr_).
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_load_balancer_waf.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/lbr_ID'
```
